source.text: וְאֵ֨לֶּה֙ דִּבְרֵ֣י הַסֵּ֔פֶר אֲשֶׁ֥ר שָׁלַ֛ח יִרְמְיָ֥ה הַנָּבִ֖יא מִירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם אֶל־יֶ֜תֶר זִקְנֵ֣י הַגּוֹלָ֗ה וְאֶל־הַכֹּהֲנִ֤ים וְאֶל־הַנְּבִיאִים֙ וְאֶל־כָּל־הָעָ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֨ר הֶגְלָ֧ה נְבֽוּכַדְנֶאצַּ֛ר מִירוּשָׁלִַ֖ם בָּבֶֽלָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And these [are the] words of the letter that sent Jeremiah the prophet from Jerusalem to [the] rest of [the] elders of the exile, and to the priests and to the prophets and to all the people whom had exiled Nebuchadnezzar from Jerusalem to Babylon,

en.L: And these [are] the words of the letter that Jeremiah the prophet sent from Jerusalem to the rest of the elders of the exiles, and to the priests and to the prophets and to all the people whom Nebuchadnezzar had exiled from Jerusalem to Babylon,
en.B: This is the text of the letter Jeremiah the prophet sent from Jerusalem to the elders who were left among the exiles, to the priests and the prophets, and to all the people Nebuchadnezzar had carried into exile from Jerusalem to Babylon,
en.R: This is the letter that Jeremiah the prophet sent from Jerusalem to the people who had been taken away to Babylon as captives. He wrote to the elders among them who were still alive, to the priests and the prophets, and to all the other people Nebuchadnezzar had taken from Jerusalem to Babylon.

es.L: Y estas [son] las palabras de la carta que el profeta Jeremías envió desde Jerusalén al resto de los ancianos del destierro, y a los sacerdotes, y a los profetas, y a todo el pueblo que Nabucodonosor había llevado cautivo de Jerusalén a Babilonia,
es.B: Este es el texto de la carta que el profeta Jeremías envió desde Jerusalén a los ancianos que quedaban entre los desterrados, a los sacerdotes y a los profetas, y a todo el pueblo que Nabucodonosor había llevado al destierro de Jerusalén a Babilonia,
es.R: Esta es la carta que el profeta Jeremías envió desde Jerusalén a la gente que había sido llevada prisionera a Babilonia. Les escribió a los ancianos que todavía vivían entre ellos, a los sacerdotes y a los profetas, y a todas las demás personas que Nabucodonosor se había llevado de Jerusalén a Babilonia.

fr.L: Et voici les paroles de la lettre que Jérémie le prophète envoya de Jérusalem au reste des anciens de l’exil, et aux prêtres, et aux prophètes, et à tout le peuple que Nabuchodonosor avait déporté de Jérusalem à Babylone,
fr.B: Voici le texte de la lettre que le prophète Jérémie envoya de Jérusalem aux anciens qui restaient parmi les exilés, aux prêtres et aux prophètes, et à tout le peuple que Nabuchodonosor avait emmené en exil de Jérusalem à Babylone,
fr.R: Voici la lettre que le prophète Jérémie a envoyée de Jérusalem aux gens qu’on avait emmenés comme prisonniers à Babylone. Il a écrit aux anciens qui étaient encore en vie parmi eux, aux prêtres et aux prophètes, et à tous les autres que Nabuchodonosor avait emmenés de Jérusalem à Babylone.

sw.L: Na haya [ndiyo] maneno ya barua ambayo Yeremia nabii aliituma kutoka Yerusalemu kwa wazee waliobaki wa mateka, na kwa makuhani, na kwa manabii, na kwa watu wote ambao Nebukadneza aliwachukua mateka kutoka Yerusalemu mpaka Babeli,
sw.B: Haya ndiyo maneno ya barua ambayo nabii Yeremia aliituma kutoka Yerusalemu kwa wazee waliobaki kati ya mateka, kwa makuhani na manabii, na kwa watu wote ambao Nebukadneza aliwachukua kutoka Yerusalemu kwenda uhamishoni Babeli,
sw.R: Hii ndiyo barua ambayo nabii Yeremia aliituma kutoka Yerusalemu kwa watu waliokuwa wamechukuliwa mateka mpaka Babeli. Aliwaandikia wazee wao waliokuwa bado hai, makuhani na manabii, na watu wengine wote ambao Nebukadneza aliwachukua kutoka Yerusalemu mpaka Babeli.

vi.L: Đây [là] những lời của bức thư mà tiên tri Giê-rê-mi gửi từ Giê-ru-sa-lem cho những trưởng lão còn lại trong số người lưu đày, cho các thầy tế lễ, các nhà tiên tri và toàn dân mà Nê-bu-cát-nết-sa đã bắt lưu đày từ Giê-ru-sa-lem qua Ba-by-lôn,
vi.B: Đây là nội dung bức thư mà tiên tri Giê-rê-mi gửi từ Giê-ru-sa-lem cho các trưởng lão còn lại trong số người lưu đày, cho các thầy tế lễ, các nhà tiên tri và toàn dân mà Nê-bu-cát-nết-sa đã bắt đi lưu đày từ Giê-ru-sa-lem qua Ba-by-lôn,
vi.R: Đây là bức thư tiên tri Giê-rê-mi gửi từ Giê-ru-sa-lem cho những người đã bị bắt qua Ba-by-lôn làm tù binh. Ông viết cho các trưởng lão còn sống trong số họ, cho các thầy tế lễ và các nhà tiên tri, cùng mọi người khác mà Nê-bu-cát-nết-sa đã bắt từ Giê-ru-sa-lem đem qua Ba-by-lôn.

ko.L: 그리고 이것은 예언자 예레미야가 예루살렘에서, 포로 가운데 남은 장로들과 제사장들과 예언자들과, 느부갓네살이 예루살렘에서 바빌론으로 사로잡아 간 모든 백성에게 보낸 편지의 말이다.
ko.B: 이것은 예언자 예레미야가 예루살렘에서 보낸 편지의 내용이다. 그는 이 편지를 포로들 가운데 남아 있는 장로들과 제사장들과 예언자들과, 느부갓네살이 예루살렘에서 바빌론으로 사로잡아 간 모든 백성에게 보냈다.
ko.R: 이것은 예언자 예레미야가 예루살렘에서 바빌론으로 포로로 끌려간 사람들에게 보낸 편지다. 그는 그들 가운데 아직 살아 있는 장로들과 제사장들과 예언자들과, 느부갓네살이 예루살렘에서 바빌론으로 끌고 간 다른 모든 백성에게 편지를 썼다.

pt.L: E estas [são] as palavras da carta que o profeta Jeremias enviou de Jerusalém ao resto dos anciãos do exílio, e aos sacerdotes, e aos profetas, e a todo o povo que Nabucodonosor tinha levado para o exílio, de Jerusalém para a Babilônia,
pt.B: Este é o texto da carta que o profeta Jeremias enviou de Jerusalém aos anciãos que tinham restado entre os exilados, aos sacerdotes e aos profetas, e a todo o povo que Nabucodonosor tinha levado de Jerusalém para o exílio na Babilônia,
pt.R: Esta é a carta que o profeta Jeremias enviou de Jerusalém às pessoas que tinham sido levadas como prisioneiras para a Babilônia. Ele escreveu aos anciãos que ainda estavam vivos entre elas, aos sacerdotes e aos profetas, e a todas as outras pessoas que Nabucodonosor tinha levado de Jerusalém para a Babilônia.

decisions.choice: the letter: a written message sent from Jerusalem to the exiles in Babylon, some years after 597 BC
decisions.reason: The word means a written document, here a letter (2 Samuel 11:14; 2 Kings 5:5). Jeremiah stayed in Jerusalem, so he sent God's word to the exiles in writing. The letter is not dated; it was sent after the exile of 597 BC (verse 2) in the reign of Zedekiah (verse 3), and it belongs with the events of chapters 27-28, which are set early in that reign.

decisions.choice: the rest of the elders: the elders who were still living, or who remained
decisions.reason: The word means what is left over. It may simply mean the elders who were there, or it may hint that some had died on the journey or since, or had been put to death (compare verses 21-22). The text does not say which.

decisions.choice: the exile: the exiles as one group
decisions.reason: The noun means "exile" and is used for the whole company of those taken away, as in 24:5.

decisions.choice: Nebuchadnezzar: the form of the name with n
decisions.reason: Chapters 27-29 mostly spell the Babylonian king's name Nebuchadnezzar, as Kings does; most of Jeremiah spells it Nebuchadrezzar, and this chapter has that form in verse 21. Both name the same king (see 25:1).

decisions.choice: the chapter's place in the Greek translation
decisions.reason: In the Greek translation (the Septuagint) this chapter is numbered 36, since the oracles against the nations come earlier there (see 1:1 and 25:13), and it is shorter: it lacks verses 16-20 and parts of other verses (see verses 14 and 16). The Hebrew is followed.

decisions.choice: Nebuchadnezzar
decisions.reason: Each verse keeps the form of the king's name its Hebrew uses (m4).

decisions.choice: the elders who were left among the exiles (Balanced); the elders among them who were still alive (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "the rest of the elders" means in ordinary English. Readable splits the verse into two sentences and calls the exiles "people taken away as captives".

decisions.choice: el destierro (Literal); los desterrados (Balanced); la gente que había sido llevada prisionera (Readable)
decisions.reason: The exiles as one group (meaning decision m3) take "destierro", the word published 24 times in Kings and Chronicles and set by the terms note for Ezra.

decisions.choice: "Nê-bu-cát-nết-sa"
decisions.reason: This verse's Hebrew has the form with n, so the published form of 2 Kings is used, as in chapters 27-28 (decision at 21:2).

decisions.choice: "느부갓네살"
decisions.reason: This chapter's Hebrew has the form with n (meaning decision m4), so Korean uses the published form of 2 Kings, as the terms note says each verse keeps its own form.

decisions.choice: Verse 1 closed as a sentence
decisions.reason: The Hebrew runs on into verses 2-3; Korean closes each verse as its own sentence so that every verse keeps its own content after its marker.

source.text: אַחֲרֵ֣י צֵ֣את יְכָנְיָֽה־הַ֠מֶּלֶךְ וְהַגְּבִירָ֨ה וְהַסָּרִיסִ֜ים שָׂרֵ֨י יְהוּדָ֧ה וִירוּשָׁלִַ֛ם וְהֶחָרָ֥שׁ וְהַמַּסְגֵּ֖ר מִירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: after went out Jeconiah the king and the queen mother and the eunuchs, [the] princes of Judah and Jerusalem, and the craftsman and the smith from Jerusalem,

en.L: after Jeconiah the king and the queen mother and the eunuchs, the princes of Judah and Jerusalem, and the craftsmen and the smiths had gone out from Jerusalem,
en.B: after King Jeconiah, the queen mother, the court officers, the officials of Judah and Jerusalem, and the craftsmen and smiths had gone from Jerusalem into exile,
en.R: This was after King Jeconiah had been taken away from Jerusalem. The king's mother, the palace officials, the leaders of Judah and Jerusalem, and the skilled workers and metalworkers had been taken with him.

es.L: después que salieron de Jerusalén el rey Jeconías, y la reina madre, y los eunucos, los príncipes de Judá y de Jerusalén, y los artesanos y los herreros,
es.B: después de que el rey Jeconías, la reina madre, los funcionarios de la corte, los jefes de Judá y de Jerusalén, y los artesanos y los herreros habían salido de Jerusalén al destierro,
es.R: Esto fue después de que se llevaron de Jerusalén al rey Jeconías. Con él se llevaron también a la madre del rey, a los funcionarios del palacio, a los dirigentes de Judá y de Jerusalén, y a los trabajadores especializados y los herreros.

fr.L: après que le roi Jéchonias, et la reine mère, et les eunuques, les princes de Juda et de Jérusalem, et les artisans et les forgerons furent sortis de Jérusalem,
fr.B: après que le roi Jéchonias, la reine mère, les hauts fonctionnaires, les chefs de Juda et de Jérusalem, les artisans et les forgerons eurent quitté Jérusalem pour l’exil,
fr.R: C’était après qu’on avait emmené le roi Jéchonias loin de Jérusalem. On avait emmené avec lui la mère du roi, les fonctionnaires du palais, les chefs de Juda et de Jérusalem, les artisans et ceux qui travaillaient les métaux.

sw.L: baada ya Yekonia mfalme, na mama wa mfalme, na matowashi, wakuu wa Yuda na Yerusalemu, na mafundi na wahunzi kutoka Yerusalemu,
sw.B: baada ya Mfalme Yekonia, mama wa mfalme, maafisa wa ikulu, maafisa wa Yuda na Yerusalemu, na mafundi na wahunzi kuondoka Yerusalemu kwenda uhamishoni,
sw.R: Hii ilikuwa baada ya Mfalme Yekonia kuchukuliwa kutoka Yerusalemu. Mama wa mfalme, maafisa wa ikulu, viongozi wa Yuda na Yerusalemu, na mafundi stadi na wafua vyuma walichukuliwa pamoja naye.

vi.L: sau khi vua Giê-chô-nia, thái hậu, các hoạn quan, các quan trưởng Giu-đa và Giê-ru-sa-lem, cùng thợ thủ công và thợ rèn đã ra khỏi Giê-ru-sa-lem,
vi.B: sau khi vua Giê-chô-nia, thái hậu, các quan chức trong cung, các quan chức Giu-đa và Giê-ru-sa-lem, cùng thợ thủ công và thợ rèn đã rời Giê-ru-sa-lem đi lưu đày,
vi.R: Việc ấy xảy ra sau khi vua Giê-chô-nia bị bắt đi khỏi Giê-ru-sa-lem. Mẹ vua, các quan chức trong cung, các nhà lãnh đạo của Giu-đa và Giê-ru-sa-lem, cùng các thợ lành nghề và thợ kim loại cũng bị bắt đi với vua.

ko.L: 그것은 여고냐 왕과 왕의 어머니와 내시들과 유다와 예루살렘의 고관들과 장인들과 대장장이들이 예루살렘에서 나간 뒤였다.
ko.B: 그때는 여고냐 왕과 왕의 어머니와 왕궁 관리들과 유다와 예루살렘의 관리들과 장인들과 대장장이들이 예루살렘에서 포로로 끌려간 뒤였다.
ko.R: 그때는 여고냐 왕이 예루살렘에서 끌려간 뒤였다. 왕의 어머니와 왕궁 관리들과 유다와 예루살렘의 지도자들과 솜씨 좋은 일꾼들과 쇠붙이를 다루는 기술자들도 그와 함께 끌려갔다.

pt.L: depois que saíram de Jerusalém o rei Jeconias, e a rainha-mãe, e os eunucos, os príncipes de Judá e de Jerusalém, e os artífices e os ferreiros,
pt.B: depois que o rei Jeconias, a rainha-mãe, os funcionários da corte, os oficiais de Judá e de Jerusalém, e os artífices e os ferreiros tinham saído de Jerusalém para o exílio,
pt.R: Isso aconteceu depois que o rei Jeconias foi levado de Jerusalém. A mãe do rei, os oficiais do palácio, os líderes de Judá e de Jerusalém, e os artesãos e os ferreiros tinham sido levados com ele.

decisions.choice: went out: left the city in surrender and went into exile
decisions.reason: Jeconiah went out of the besieged city to the king of Babylon and gave himself up, and he and his court were carried off (2 Kings 24:12, 15).

decisions.choice: the queen mother: the king's mother, who held an honored place at court
decisions.reason: The title means "great lady". The king's mother had a rank of her own (13:18; 22:26; 1 Kings 2:19). Jeconiah's mother was Nehushta (2 Kings 24:8), and she was taken to Babylon with him (2 Kings 24:12, 15).

decisions.choice: the eunuchs: royal court officials, perhaps castrated men
decisions.reason: As in 2 Kings 24:12, the word names a class of court officers. Many such officers in the courts of the ancient Near East were castrated, but the word is also used of high officials who were not.

decisions.choice: the same groups as in 2 Kings 24:12-16 and Jeremiah 24:1
decisions.reason: Kings lists the king, his mother, his servants, princes and eunuchs, the leading men, the warriors, the craftsmen and the smiths (2 Kings 24:12-16); Jeremiah 24:1 names the same king, the princes and the two trades. Jeconiah is the king called Jehoiachin in Kings and Coniah in 22:24. The princes are here called "of Judah and Jerusalem".

decisions.choice: eunuchs, princes (Literal); court officers, officials (Balanced); palace officials, leaders (Readable); craftsmen and smiths (Readable: skilled workers and metalworkers)
decisions.reason: Worded as in 2 Kings 24:12-16. Balanced uses "officials" for the princes, as usual in these books, so it calls the eunuchs "court officers" to keep the two groups apart; Readable has "leaders" and "palace officials".

decisions.choice: had gone from Jerusalem into exile (Balanced); had been taken away (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "went out" meant here (m1). Readable starts a new sentence and says "with him" for the list of those taken.

decisions.choice: eunucos (Literal); funcionarios de la corte (Balanced); funcionarios del palacio (Readable)
decisions.reason: *Saris* keeps the wording the terms note sets: "eunuco" at Literal, "funcionario" at Balanced and Readable.

decisions.choice: matowashi (Literal); maafisa wa ikulu (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: *Saris* at each level as the Kings note sets ("matowashi" at Literal, officials at Balanced and Readable), worded "maafisa wa ikulu" throughout Jeremiah (34:19; 38:7; 41:16).

decisions.choice: "les eunuques" (L), "les hauts fonctionnaires" (B), "les fonctionnaires du palais" (R); "les princes" (L), "les chefs" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The French wording of saris and sar as the Kings note and 2 Kings 24:12 set them.

decisions.choice: "hoạn quan" (L); "triều thần" (B); "quan chức trong cung" (R) for saris
decisions.reason: The terms note's pattern for saris, matching the published 2 Kings 24:12 ("hoạn quan" / "triều thần"); "thái hậu" names the queen mother's rank at Literal and Balanced, and Readable says "mẹ vua".

decisions.choice: "왕의 어머니"; "내시들" (L), "왕궁 관리들" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As published in 2 Kings 24:12-15 for the same group (meaning decision m4), and the terms note's forms for *saris*.

decisions.choice: a rainha-mãe; os eunucos (L), os funcionários da corte (B), os oficiais do palácio (R)
decisions.reason: The groups are worded as 2 Kings 24:12-16 has them in Portuguese (m4): Literal keeps "eunucos" (m3), Balanced and Readable say what these men did at court. "A rainha-mãe" is the Portuguese title for the king's mother at court (m2); Readable says "a mãe do rei", as the English does.

source.text: בְּיַד֙ אֶלְעָשָׂ֣ה בֶן־שָׁפָ֔ן וּגְמַרְיָ֖ה בֶּן־חִלְקִיָּ֑ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר שָׁלַ֜ח צִדְקִיָּ֣ה מֶֽלֶךְ־יְהוּדָ֗ה אֶל־נְבוּכַדְנֶאצַּ֛ר מֶ֥לֶךְ בָּבֶ֖ל בָּבֶ֥לָה לֵאמֹֽר׃ס

records.literal_gloss: by [the] hand of Elasah son of Shaphan and Gemariah son of Hilkiah, whom sent Zedekiah king of Judah to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon [to] Babylon, saying:

en.L: by the hand of Elasah son of Shaphan and Gemariah son of Hilkiah, whom Zedekiah king of Judah sent to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, to Babylon, saying:
en.B: sending it by Elasah son of Shaphan and Gemariah son of Hilkiah. Zedekiah king of Judah had sent these two men to Babylon, to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon. The letter said:
en.R: Jeremiah gave the letter to Elasah son of Shaphan and Gemariah son of Hilkiah. Zedekiah king of Judah was sending them to Babylon to see Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon. The letter said:

es.L: por mano de Elasa hijo de Safán y de Gemarías hijo de Hilcías, a quienes Sedequías, rey de Judá, envió a Nabucodonosor, rey de Babilonia, a Babilonia, diciendo:
es.B: La envió por medio de Elasa hijo de Safán y de Gemarías hijo de Hilcías, a quienes Sedequías, rey de Judá, había enviado a Babilonia, a Nabucodonosor, rey de Babilonia. La carta decía:
es.R: Jeremías les dio la carta a Elasa hijo de Safán y a Gemarías hijo de Hilcías. Sedequías, rey de Judá, los enviaba a Babilonia para ver a Nabucodonosor, rey de Babilonia. La carta decía:

fr.L: par la main d’Éléasa fils de Shaphân et de Guemaria fils de Hilqiya, que Sédécias, roi de Juda, envoya à Nabuchodonosor, roi de Babylone, à Babylone ; elle disait :
fr.B: par l’intermédiaire d’Éléasa fils de Shaphân et de Guemaria fils de Hilqiya. Sédécias, roi de Juda, avait envoyé ces deux hommes à Babylone, auprès de Nabuchodonosor, roi de Babylone. La lettre disait :
fr.R: Jérémie a confié la lettre à Éléasa, fils de Shaphân, et à Guemaria, fils de Hilqiya. Sédécias, roi de Juda, les envoyait à Babylone pour rencontrer Nabuchodonosor, le roi de Babylone. La lettre disait :

sw.L: kwa mkono wa Elasa mwana wa Shafani na Gemaria mwana wa Hilkia, ambao Sedekia mfalme wa Yuda aliwatuma kwa Nebukadneza mfalme wa Babeli, huko Babeli, kusema:
sw.B: akaipeleka kupitia Elasa mwana wa Shafani na Gemaria mwana wa Hilkia. Sedekia mfalme wa Yuda alikuwa amewatuma watu hao wawili Babeli, kwa Nebukadneza mfalme wa Babeli. Barua ilisema:
sw.R: Yeremia aliwapa barua hiyo Elasa mwana wa Shafani na Gemaria mwana wa Hilkia. Sedekia mfalme wa Yuda alikuwa akiwatuma Babeli kuonana na Nebukadneza mfalme wa Babeli. Barua ilisema:

vi.L: qua tay Ê-lê-a-sa con trai Sa-phan và Ghê-ma-ria con trai Hinh-kia, là những người Sê-đê-kia vua Giu-đa sai đến Nê-bu-cát-nết-sa vua Ba-by-lôn, tại Ba-by-lôn. Thư viết rằng:
vi.B: Ông gửi thư qua Ê-lê-a-sa con trai Sa-phan và Ghê-ma-ria con trai Hinh-kia. Sê-đê-kia vua Giu-đa đã sai hai người này qua Ba-by-lôn gặp Nê-bu-cát-nết-sa vua Ba-by-lôn. Thư viết:

ko.L: 유다 왕 시드기야가 바빌론으로 바빌론 왕 느부갓네살에게 보낸 사반의 아들 엘라사와 힐기야의 아들 그마랴의 손을 통해 [보냈다]. [그 편지에 이렇게 쓰여 있었다].
ko.B: 그는 사반의 아들 엘라사와 힐기야의 아들 그마랴 편에 편지를 보냈다. 유다 왕 시드기야가 이 두 사람을 바빌론으로, 바빌론 왕 느부갓네살에게 보냈던 것이다. 편지에는 이렇게 쓰여 있었다.
ko.R: 예레미야는 사반의 아들 엘라사와 힐기야의 아들 그마랴에게 편지를 맡겼다. 유다 왕 시드기야가 그들을 바빌론으로 보내 바빌론 왕 느부갓네살을 만나게 했던 것이다. 편지의 내용은 이러했다.

pt.L: pela mão de Elasa, filho de Safã, e de Gemarias, filho de Hilquias, que Zedequias, rei de Judá, enviou a Nabucodonosor, rei da Babilônia, à Babilônia, dizendo:
pt.B: enviando-a por meio de Elasa, filho de Safã, e de Gemarias, filho de Hilquias. Zedequias, rei de Judá, tinha enviado esses dois homens à Babilônia, a Nabucodonosor, rei da Babilônia. A carta dizia:
pt.R: Jeremias entregou a carta a Elasa, filho de Safã, e a Gemarias, filho de Hilquias. Zedequias, rei de Judá, estava mandando os dois à Babilônia para falar com Nabucodonosor, rei da Babilônia. A carta dizia:

decisions.choice: by the hand of: carried by
decisions.reason: To send something "by the hand of" someone is to have that person carry it. The two men were travelling to Babylon on the king's business and took Jeremiah's letter with them.

decisions.choice: Elasah son of Shaphan: probably of the family that supported Jeremiah
decisions.reason: Shaphan was King Josiah's scribe (2 Kings 22:3-14). His son Ahikam protected Jeremiah when his life was in danger (26:24), and another son, Gemariah, and a grandson heard Baruch's scroll and tried to keep it from being burned (36:10-12, 25). Elasah is probably another of Shaphan's sons, though the text does not say so.

decisions.choice: Gemariah son of Hilkiah: a different man from Gemariah son of Shaphan
decisions.reason: This Gemariah is not the son of Shaphan in 36:10. His father Hilkiah may be the high priest who found the book of the law under Josiah (2 Kings 22:4-8), but the name was common, and Jeremiah's own father was a Hilkiah (1:1).

decisions.choice: whom Zedekiah sent to Nebuchadnezzar: envoys of a king who ruled under Babylon
decisions.reason: Nebuchadnezzar had made Zedekiah king (2 Kings 24:17), and Zedekiah owed him loyalty and tribute. The text does not say why he sent these men, perhaps to pay tribute or to assure the king of his loyalty after the talk of revolt in chapter 27. Zedekiah himself went, or sent an officer, to Babylon in his fourth year (51:59).

decisions.choice: saying: the letter follows, from verse 4 to verse 23
decisions.reason: The word introduces the words of the letter. It is God's message, set out as "Thus says the LORD", and it ends at verse 23.

decisions.choice: The letter said:
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable introduce the letter with a short sentence of its own. Balanced continues the sentence with "sending it by"; Readable starts new sentences and says that the envoys were going "to see" the king.

decisions.choice: "Éléasa fils de Shaphân", "Guemaria fils de Hilqiya"
decisions.reason: The French forms used for these names in Chronicles and Kings (Éléasa, Shaphân, Hilqiya).

decisions.choice: "Ê-lê-a-sa con trai Sa-phan"; "Ghê-ma-ria con trai Hinh-kia"
decisions.reason: "Sa-phan" and "Hinh-kia" are the published forms (2 Chronicles 34); "Ê-lê-a-sa" and "Ghê-ma-ria" are made the same way and are new.

decisions.choice: "사반의 아들 엘라사"; "힐기야의 아들 그마랴"
decisions.reason: Published forms of the family names (사반, 힐기야, 2 Kings 22) and the usual Korean forms of Elasah and Gemariah.

source.text: כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֛ר יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל לְכָל־הַ֨גּוֹלָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־הִגְלֵ֥יתִי מִירוּשָׁלִַ֖ם בָּבֶֽלָה׃

records.literal_gloss: Thus says Yahweh of hosts, [the] God of Israel, to all the exile whom I exiled from Jerusalem to Babylon:

en.L: "Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts, the God of Israel, to all the exiles whom I have exiled from Jerusalem to Babylon:
en.B: "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, the God of Israel, says this to all the exiles whom I sent into exile from Jerusalem to Babylon:
en.R: "This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, the God of Israel, says to all the people I sent away from Jerusalem to Babylon as captives:

es.L: «Así dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los ejércitos, el Dios de Israel, a todos los del destierro que hice llevar cautivos de Jerusalén a Babilonia:
es.B: «{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos, el Dios de Israel, dice esto a todos los desterrados que yo envié al destierro de Jerusalén a Babilonia:
es.R: «Esto es lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos, el Dios de Israel, a toda la gente que yo envié prisionera de Jerusalén a Babilonia:

fr.L: « Ainsi parle {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées, le Dieu d’Israël, à tous les exilés que j’ai déportés de Jérusalem à Babylone :
fr.B: « {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées, le Dieu d’Israël, dit ceci à tous les exilés que j’ai envoyés en exil de Jérusalem à Babylone :
fr.R: « Voici ce que dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées, le Dieu d’Israël, à tous ceux que j’ai envoyés comme prisonniers de Jérusalem à Babylone :

sw.L: "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi, Mungu wa Israeli, asema hivi kwa mateka wote niliowahamisha kutoka Yerusalemu mpaka Babeli:
sw.B: "Hivi ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi, Mungu wa Israeli, asemavyo kwa mateka wote niliowapeleka uhamishoni kutoka Yerusalemu mpaka Babeli:
sw.R: "Hili ndilo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi, Mungu wa Israeli, analosema kwa watu wote niliowapeleka kutoka Yerusalemu mpaka Babeli kama mateka:

vi.L: "{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân, Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên, phán thế này với mọi người lưu đày mà {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã bắt lưu đày từ Giê-ru-sa-lem qua Ba-by-lôn:
vi.B: "{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân, Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên, phán như vầy với mọi người lưu đày mà {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã đày từ Giê-ru-sa-lem qua Ba-by-lôn:
vi.R: "Đây là lời {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân, Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên, phán với mọi người mà {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã đưa từ Giê-ru-sa-lem qua Ba-by-lôn làm tù binh:

ko.L: "이스라엘의 하나님 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 내가 예루살렘에서 바빌론으로 사로잡아 가게 한 모든 포로에게 이와 같이 말씀하신다.
ko.B: "이스라엘의 하나님 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서, 내가 예루살렘에서 바빌론으로 사로잡혀 가게 한 모든 포로에게 이렇게 말씀하신다.
ko.R: "이스라엘의 하나님, 하늘의 군대를 거느리신 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서, 내가 예루살렘에서 바빌론으로 포로로 보낸 모든 사람에게 하시는 말씀이다.

pt.L: "Assim diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos, o Deus de Israel, a todos os exilados que eu levei para o exílio, de Jerusalém para a Babilônia:
pt.B: "Assim diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos, o Deus de Israel, a todos os exilados que eu mandei para o exílio, de Jerusalém para a Babilônia:
pt.R: "É isto que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos, o Deus de Israel, diz a todas as pessoas que eu mandei de Jerusalém para a Babilônia como prisioneiras:

decisions.choice: whom I have exiled: the exile was God's own act
decisions.reason: Verse 1 says that Nebuchadnezzar exiled them; here God says that he himself did it. Babylon was the instrument of his judgment, and the same God will bring them back (verses 10-14; 24:5).

decisions.choice: the letter speaks in God's voice from here to verse 23
decisions.reason: The letter is Jeremiah's, but its words are God's, spoken in the first person. The quotation of the letter runs to the end of verse 23.

decisions.choice: Thus says the LORD of hosts (Literal); The LORD of Armies ... says this (Balanced); This is what the LORD of Armies ... says (Readable)
decisions.reason: The wording set for this formula in Isaiah and Jeremiah (see Isaiah 1:9 on "hosts").

decisions.choice: an opening quotation mark
decisions.reason: The letter is quoted, so it opens with a quotation mark here and closes at the end of verse 23. God's words inside it take no further marks, as in 7:3.

decisions.choice: « » for the letter
decisions.reason: The letter, in God's voice to verse 23, is quoted with « »; words quoted inside it take “ ”.

decisions.choice: the letter in « », from here to verse 23; God's words inside it take no further marks
decisions.reason: As the English: the letter is quoted, and the LORD speaks in it in his own voice.

decisions.choice: God says "các ngươi" to the exiles
decisions.reason: The letter is God's word to the people as a group (meaning decision m2), so it takes the terms note's "các ngươi" at every level, even where the words are full of hope (verses 10-14).

decisions.choice: The letter opens with the prophet's formula and the honorific, then God speaks in the plain style ("내가 ... 사로잡아 가게 한")
decisions.reason: The letter is Jeremiah's own, so its formula takes the honorific as an oracle does; God's "I" begins inside the same sentence (meaning decision m1), as in the Hebrew.

records.literal_gloss: Build houses and dwell, and plant gardens and eat their produce.

en.L: Build houses and live [in them]; and plant gardens and eat their produce.
en.B: Build houses and settle down in them. Plant gardens and eat what they produce.
en.R: Build houses and live in them. Plant gardens and eat the food they grow.

es.L: {{plural_you:Edifiquen|Edificad}} casas y {{plural_you:habiten|habitad}} [en ellas]; y {{plural_you:planten|plantad}} huertos y {{plural_you:coman|comed}} su fruto.
es.B: {{plural_you:Construyan|Construid}} casas y {{plural_you:establézcanse|estableceos}} en ellas. {{plural_you:Planten|Plantad}} huertos y {{plural_you:coman|comed}} de lo que producen.
es.R: {{plural_you:Construyan|Construid}} casas y {{plural_you:vivan|vivid}} en ellas. {{plural_you:Planten|Plantad}} huertos y {{plural_you:coman|comed}} lo que crezca en ellos.

fr.L: Bâtissez des maisons et habitez[-les] ; plantez des jardins et mangez-en le fruit.
fr.B: Bâtissez des maisons et installez-vous-y. Plantez des jardins et mangez ce qu’ils produisent.
fr.R: Construisez des maisons et habitez-les. Plantez des jardins et mangez ce qui y pousse.

sw.L: Jengeni nyumba mkae [ndani yake]; pandeni bustani mle matunda yake.
sw.B: Jengeni nyumba mkatulie ndani yake. Pandeni bustani mle mazao yake.
sw.R: Jengeni nyumba mkaishi ndani yake. Pandeni bustani mle chakula kinachoota humo.

vi.L: Hãy xây nhà mà ở; hãy trồng vườn và ăn hoa quả của vườn.
vi.B: Hãy xây nhà và định cư ở đó. Hãy trồng vườn và ăn hoa quả vườn sinh ra.
vi.R: Hãy xây nhà và ở trong đó. Hãy trồng vườn và ăn rau trái vườn sinh ra.

ko.L: 집을 짓고 [그 안에] 살아라. 그리고 밭을 일구고 그 열매를 먹어라.
ko.B: 집을 짓고 그곳에 자리 잡고 살아라. 텃밭을 가꾸고 거기서 나는 것을 먹어라.
ko.R: 집을 짓고 거기서 살아라. 텃밭을 가꾸어 거기서 기른 것을 먹어라.

pt.L: Construam casas e habitem [nelas]; e plantem pomares e comam o seu fruto.
pt.B: Construam casas e se instalem nelas. Plantem pomares e comam o que eles produzirem.
pt.R: Construam casas e morem nelas. Plantem pomares e comam o que eles produzirem.

decisions.choice: build and live, plant and eat: the curse of Deuteronomy 28:30 turned around
decisions.reason: Moses warned that if Israel broke the covenant they would build houses and not live in them, and plant vineyards and not enjoy their fruit (Deuteronomy 28:30, 39). In exile, the very place of that curse, God tells his people to build and live, plant and eat. The verbs "build" and "plant" also recall Jeremiah's call (1:10).

decisions.choice: live: settle and stay
decisions.reason: The verb means to sit, to dwell, to stay. With "build houses" it means to make a settled home, not to wait for a quick return; verse 28 sums the advice up as "It will be long".

decisions.choice: gardens: plots of vegetables and fruit trees
decisions.reason: A garden was an enclosed plot of fruit trees and vegetables. Planting one meant waiting for years of harvests.

decisions.choice: [in them] (Literal); settle down in them (Balanced)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "dwell"; English needs to say where. Balanced says "settle down" to bring out m2.

decisions.choice: construam ... habitem, plantem ... comam; pomares
decisions.reason: The commands turn round the curse of Deuteronomy 28:30 (m1), and keep the verbs that verse has in Portuguese, "construir", "morar/habitar", "plantar". The gardens are plots of fruit trees and vegetables (m3), so "pomares", where Portuguese "jardins" would suggest flowers.

records.literal_gloss: Take wives and father sons and daughters, and take for your sons wives, and your daughters give to husbands, and they will bear sons and daughters; and multiply there, and not become few.

en.L: Take wives and father sons and daughters, and take wives for your sons and give your daughters to husbands, so that they may bear sons and daughters; and multiply there, and do not become few.
en.B: Marry and have sons and daughters. Find wives for your sons and give your daughters to husbands, so that they in turn have sons and daughters. Increase in number there; do not decrease.
en.R: Get married and have children. Find wives for your sons and husbands for your daughters, so that they also have children. Grow in number there. Do not let your numbers get smaller.

es.L: {{plural_you:Tomen|Tomad}} mujeres y {{plural_you:engendren|engendrad}} hijos e hijas; {{plural_you:tomen|tomad}} mujeres para {{plural_you:sus hijos|vuestros hijos}} y {{plural_you:den sus hijas|dad vuestras hijas}} a maridos, para que den a luz hijos e hijas; y {{plural_you:multiplíquense|multiplicaos}} allí, y no {{plural_you:disminuyan|disminuyáis}}.
es.B: {{plural_you:Cásense|Casaos}} y {{plural_you:tengan|tened}} hijos e hijas. {{plural_you:Busquen|Buscad}} esposas para {{plural_you:sus hijos|vuestros hijos}} y {{plural_you:den sus hijas|dad vuestras hijas}} en matrimonio, para que ellos a su vez tengan hijos e hijas. {{plural_you:Aumenten|Aumentad}} en número allí; no {{plural_you:disminuyan|disminuyáis}}.
es.R: {{plural_you:Cásense|Casaos}} y {{plural_you:tengan|tened}} hijos. {{plural_you:Busquen|Buscad}} esposas para {{plural_you:sus hijos|vuestros hijos}} y maridos para {{plural_you:sus hijas|vuestras hijas}}, para que ellos también tengan hijos. {{plural_you:Crezcan|Creced}} en número allí. No {{plural_you:dejen|dejéis}} que {{plural_you:su número|vuestro número}} disminuya.

fr.L: Prenez des femmes et engendrez des fils et des filles ; prenez des femmes pour vos fils et donnez vos filles à des maris, afin qu’elles enfantent des fils et des filles ; multipliez-vous là-bas, et ne diminuez pas.
fr.B: Mariez-vous et ayez des fils et des filles. Trouvez des femmes pour vos fils et donnez vos filles en mariage, afin qu’ils aient à leur tour des fils et des filles. Multipliez-vous là-bas ; ne diminuez pas.
fr.R: Mariez-vous et ayez des enfants. Trouvez des femmes pour vos fils et des maris pour vos filles, pour qu’ils aient eux aussi des enfants. Devenez nombreux là-bas. Ne laissez pas votre nombre diminuer.

sw.L: Oeni wake mzae wana na binti, mkawaoze wana wenu wake na kuwaoza binti zenu kwa waume, ili wazae wana na binti; mkaongezeke huko, wala msipungue.
sw.B: Oeni, mzae wana na binti. Watafutieni wana wenu wake, na binti zenu muwaoze kwa waume, ili nao wazae wana na binti. Ongezekeni huko; msipungue.
sw.R: Oeni na kuolewa, mzae watoto. Watafutieni wana wenu wake na binti zenu waume, ili nao wazae watoto. Ongezekeni idadi huko. Msikubali idadi yenu ipungue.

vi.L: Hãy cưới vợ và sinh con trai con gái; hãy cưới vợ cho con trai các ngươi và gả con gái các ngươi cho chồng, để chúng sinh con trai con gái; hãy gia tăng ở đó, đừng để bị giảm sút.
vi.B: Hãy lấy vợ và sinh con trai con gái. Hãy cưới vợ cho con trai và gả con gái cho chồng, để chúng cũng sinh con trai con gái. Hãy gia tăng ở đó, đừng để giảm sút.
vi.R: Hãy lập gia đình và sinh con cái. Hãy cưới vợ cho con trai và gả chồng cho con gái, để chúng cũng có con cái. Hãy sinh sôi nảy nở ở đó. Đừng để số người của các ngươi ít đi.

ko.L: 아내를 맞아 아들딸을 낳고, 너희 아들들에게 아내를 맞아 주고 너희 딸들을 남편에게 주어, 그들도 아들딸을 낳게 하여라. 그리고 거기에서 번성하고 줄어들지 마라.
ko.B: 결혼하여 아들딸을 낳아라. 너희 아들들에게 아내를 얻어 주고 너희 딸들을 시집보내어, 그들도 아들딸을 낳게 하여라. 그곳에서 수가 늘어나게 하고 줄어들지 않게 하여라.
ko.R: 결혼해서 자녀를 낳아라. 아들들에게는 아내를, 딸들에게는 남편을 찾아 주어서, 그들도 자녀를 낳게 하여라. 그곳에서 수가 늘어나게 하여라. 줄어들지 않게 하여라.

pt.L: Tomem mulheres e gerem filhos e filhas, e tomem mulheres para os seus filhos, e deem as suas filhas a maridos, para que deem à luz filhos e filhas; e multipliquem-se ali, e não diminuam.
pt.B: Casem-se e tenham filhos e filhas. Arranjem esposas para os seus filhos e deem as suas filhas em casamento, para que também eles tenham filhos e filhas. Multipliquem-se ali; não diminuam.
pt.R: Casem-se e tenham filhos. Arranjem esposas para os seus filhos e maridos para as suas filhas, para que eles também tenham filhos. Aumentem em número ali. Não deixem o seu número diminuir.

decisions.choice: multiply there: the blessing of increase, even in exile
decisions.reason: "Be fruitful and multiply" is the blessing given at creation and after the flood (Genesis 1:28; 9:1), and Israel multiplied in Egypt even while it was oppressed (Exodus 1:7, 12). The exile is not to be the end of the people; they are to grow in number until God brings them back.

decisions.choice: take wives for your sons, give your daughters to husbands: parents arranged their children's marriages
decisions.reason: Fathers arranged marriages for their sons and daughters (Genesis 24:3-4; 34:8-9). The command reaches two generations: the exiles' grandchildren will be born in Babylon, which agrees with the seventy years of verse 10.

decisions.choice: and they will bear: so that they may bear
decisions.reason: The verb continues the commands and gives their purpose or result: the daughters given in marriage will in turn have children.

decisions.choice: Marry (Balanced); have children (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Take wives" is the Hebrew way of saying "marry". Readable says "children" for "sons and daughters", which means the same.

records.literal_gloss: And seek [the] peace of the city where I exiled you there, and pray on its behalf to Yahweh, for in its peace will be to you peace.

en.L: And seek the peace of the city where I have exiled you, and pray to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} on its behalf, for in its peace there will be peace for you.
en.B: Seek the peace of the city where I have sent you as exiles, and pray to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for it, since your own peace depends on its peace.
en.R: Work for the well-being of the city where I have sent you as captives. Pray to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for it. If the city is at peace and doing well, you will be too.

es.L: Y {{plural_you:busquen|buscad}} la paz de la ciudad adonde {{plural_you:los|os}} he llevado cautivos, y {{plural_you:rueguen|rogad}} por ella {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, porque en su paz {{plural_you:tendrán|tendréis}} paz.
es.B: {{plural_you:Busquen|Buscad}} la paz de la ciudad adonde {{plural_you:los|os}} he enviado al destierro, y {{plural_you:oren|orad}} {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} por ella, porque de su paz depende {{plural_you:su propia paz|vuestra propia paz}}.
es.R: {{plural_you:Trabajen|Trabajad}} por el bienestar de la ciudad adonde {{plural_you:los|os}} he enviado como prisioneros. {{plural_you:Oren|Orad}} {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} por ella. Si a la ciudad le va bien y vive en paz, a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} también {{plural_you:les|os}} irá bien.

fr.L: Et recherchez la paix de la ville où je vous ai déportés, et priez {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} en sa faveur, car dans sa paix vous aurez la paix.
fr.B: Recherchez la paix de la ville où je vous ai envoyés en exil, et priez {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} pour elle, car votre paix dépend de sa paix.
fr.R: Travaillez au bien-être de la ville où je vous ai envoyés comme prisonniers. Priez {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} pour elle. Si la ville est en paix et prospère, vous le serez aussi.

sw.L: Na mtafuteni amani ya mji ule niliowahamishia, mkauombee kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, kwa maana katika amani yake ninyi mtakuwa na amani.
sw.B: Itafuteni amani ya mji ule niliowapeleka kama mateka, na kuuombea kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, kwa kuwa amani yenu inategemea amani yake.
sw.R: Fanyeni kazi kwa ajili ya ustawi wa mji ule niliowapeleka kama mateka. Mwombeni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} kwa ajili yake. Mji ukiwa na amani na ukistawi, nanyi mtastawi.

vi.L: Hãy tìm cầu bình an cho thành mà {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã đày các ngươi đến, và hãy cầu nguyện {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} cho thành ấy, vì trong sự bình an của thành ấy, các ngươi sẽ được bình an.
vi.B: Hãy tìm cầu bình an cho thành mà {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã đày các ngươi đến, và hãy cầu nguyện với {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} cho thành ấy, vì thành ấy được bình an thì các ngươi cũng được bình an.
vi.R: Hãy làm cho thành mà {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã đưa các ngươi đến làm tù binh được thịnh vượng. Hãy cầu nguyện với {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} cho thành ấy. Nếu thành ấy được yên ổn và thịnh vượng, thì các ngươi cũng vậy.

ko.L: 그리고 내가 너희를 사로잡혀 가게 한 그 성의 평안을 구하고, 그 성을 위하여 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}에게 기도하여라. 그 성이 평안해야 너희도 평안할 것이다.
ko.B: 내가 너희를 포로로 보낸 그 성이 평안하도록 힘쓰고, 그 성을 위하여 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}에게 기도하여라. 그 성이 평안해야 너희도 평안하기 때문이다.
ko.R: 내가 너희를 포로로 보낸 그 성이 잘되도록 힘써라. 그 성을 위해 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}에게 기도하여라. 그 성이 평안하고 잘되면 너희도 그렇게 될 것이다.

pt.L: E busquem a paz da cidade para onde eu os levei para o exílio, e orem por ela {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}}, pois na paz dela vocês terão paz.
pt.B: Busquem a paz da cidade para onde eu os mandei como exilados e orem {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}} por ela, porque a paz de vocês depende da paz dela.
pt.R: Trabalhem pelo bem-estar da cidade para onde eu os mandei como prisioneiros. Orem {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}} por ela. Se a cidade estiver em paz e tudo correr bem com ela, tudo vai correr bem com vocês também.

decisions.choice: peace: the city's whole well-being, its safety, order and prosperity
decisions.reason: The word means wholeness and well-being of every kind: safety from war, order, health and plenty, as well as good relations between people. The exiles are to seek all of this for the city they live in. The word comes three times, so that the city's well-being and the exiles' own are bound together. Jeremiah has spoken against prophets who promised "peace" to Jerusalem when there was none (6:14; 8:11; 14:13); here God himself tells the exiles to seek it for Babylon.

decisions.choice: pray to the LORD for it: prayer for the city of the conquerors
decisions.reason: The exiles are told to pray for a foreign city, the seat of the empire that had taken them captive. This is not the same as giving up hope of return (verses 10-14). Other exiles cried out against Babylon (Psalm 137:8-9); this letter tells them to pray for its good while they live there.

decisions.choice: seek: work for, actively pursue
decisions.reason: The verb means to seek, to inquire after, to care for. It is the same verb used for seeking God in verse 13: they are to seek the good of the city and seek the LORD.

decisions.choice: the city where I have exiled you: wherever the exiles live
decisions.reason: The singular may mean Babylon itself or each town where exiles were settled; Ezekiel lived among exiles at Tel-abib by the river Chebar (Ezekiel 3:15). God again calls himself the one who exiled them (verse 4).

decisions.choice: peace (all three times)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the settled word "peace" and use it all three times, so the link between the city's peace and the exiles' peace stays visible; m1 says how wide the word is.

decisions.choice: well-being; at peace and doing well; you will be too
decisions.reason: Readable says "well-being" first, so that readers do not take the word to mean only the absence of war, and then puts the link between the city and the exiles in a plain "if ... then" sentence.

decisions.choice: paz (all three times)
decisions.reason: *Shalom* is the city's whole well-being (meaning decision m1). Literal and Balanced keep "paz" three times, as the Hebrew repeats it; Readable says "bienestar" and "le va bien".

decisions.choice: amani (three times)
decisions.reason: *Shalom* is "amani" all three times at Literal and Balanced, so the repetition is heard; Readable says "ustawi" (well-being) and "amani na ... kustawi", as the English Readable widens the word.

decisions.choice: "la paix" three times (L, B); "le bien-être" (R)
decisions.reason: As the English: Literal and Balanced keep the one word three times so that the link stays visible; Readable says "bien-être" so that readers do not take it to mean only the absence of war.

decisions.choice: "bình an" three times (L, B); "thịnh vượng", "yên ổn" (R)
decisions.reason: "Bình an" is the key term for shalom, kept all three times at Literal and Balanced so the link is heard; Readable names the city's whole well-being, as meaning decision m1 describes.

decisions.choice: "평안" three times (L, B); "잘되다", "평안하고 잘되다" (R)
decisions.reason: *shalom* here is the city's whole well-being (meaning decision m1); "평안" covers safety and welfare, and Literal and Balanced keep the one word three times, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}에게 기도하여라", with the plain particle in God's mouth
decisions.reason: God speaks of prayer to the LORD in the third person; by the one rule for Isaiah, Jeremiah and Ezra, God names himself without the honorific (no -시-, no 께) except inside words quoted from people (as Isa 66:5), as at 28:16 and 29:32.

decisions.choice: a paz (three times, L, B); o bem-estar (R)
decisions.reason: Shalom is the city's whole well-being (m1), and Literal and Balanced keep "paz" all three times, as the English does, so the reader sees that the exiles' peace is bound to the city's; Readable says "bem-estar" first, as the English Readable says "well-being", and verse 11 takes up the same word.

source.text: כִּי֩ כֹ֨ה אָמַ֜ר יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אַל־יַשִּׁ֧יאוּ לָכֶ֛ם נְבִֽיאֵיכֶ֥ם אֲשֶׁר־בְּקִרְבְּכֶ֖ם וְקֹֽסְמֵיכֶ֑ם וְאַֽל־תִּשְׁמְעוּ֙ אֶל־חֲלֹמֹ֣תֵיכֶ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר אַתֶּ֖ם מַחְלְמִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: For thus says Yahweh of hosts, [the] God of Israel: Not let deceive you your prophets who [are] in your midst and your diviners, and not listen to your dreams which you [are] causing to dream.

en.L: For thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts, the God of Israel: Do not let your prophets who [are] among you and your diviners deceive you, and do not listen to your dreams, which you are causing [them] to dream.
en.B: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, the God of Israel, says this: Do not let the prophets and the diviners who are among you deceive you, and do not listen to the dreams that you urge them to dream.
en.R: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, the God of Israel, says: Do not let the prophets and the fortune-tellers among you fool you. Do not listen to the dreams that you want them to dream for you.

es.L: Porque así dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los ejércitos, el Dios de Israel: No {{plural_you:los|os}} engañen {{plural_you:sus profetas|vuestros profetas}} que [están] entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, ni {{plural_you:sus adivinos|vuestros adivinos}}, y no {{plural_you:escuchen|escuchéis}} {{plural_you:sus sueños|vuestros sueños}}, los que {{plural_you:ustedes les hacen|vosotros les hacéis}} soñar.
es.B: Porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos, el Dios de Israel, dice esto: No {{plural_you:dejen|dejéis}} que {{plural_you:los|os}} engañen los profetas y los adivinos que hay entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, y no {{plural_you:hagan|hagáis}} caso de los sueños que {{plural_you:ustedes les piden|vosotros les pedís}} que sueñen.
es.R: Esto es lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos, el Dios de Israel: No {{plural_you:dejen|dejéis}} que {{plural_you:los|os}} engañen los profetas y los adivinos que hay entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. No {{plural_you:hagan|hagáis}} caso de los sueños que {{plural_you:ustedes quieren|vosotros queréis}} que tengan.

fr.L: Car ainsi parle {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées, le Dieu d’Israël : Que vos prophètes qui [sont] au milieu de vous et vos devins ne vous trompent pas, et n’écoutez pas vos songes, que vous [leur] faites songer.
fr.B: Car {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées, le Dieu d’Israël, dit ceci : Ne vous laissez pas tromper par les prophètes et les devins qui sont parmi vous, et n’écoutez pas les rêves que vous les poussez à faire.
fr.R: Voici ce que dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées, le Dieu d’Israël : Ne vous laissez pas avoir par les prophètes et les diseurs de bonne aventure qui sont parmi vous. N’écoutez pas les rêves que vous voulez qu’ils fassent pour vous.

sw.L: Kwa maana {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi, Mungu wa Israeli, asema hivi: Manabii wenu walio kati yenu, na waaguzi wenu, wasiwadanganye, wala msizisikilize ndoto zenu mnazowaotesha.
sw.B: Kwa maana hivi ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi, Mungu wa Israeli, asemavyo: Msiwaache manabii na waaguzi walio kati yenu wawadanganye, wala msizisikilize ndoto mnazowahimiza waote.
sw.R: Hili ndilo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi, Mungu wa Israeli, analosema: Msiwaache manabii na wapiga ramli walio kati yenu wawadanganye. Msisikilize ndoto mnazotaka wawaotee.

vi.L: Vì {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân, Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên, phán thế này: Đừng để các nhà tiên tri ở giữa các ngươi và các thầy bói của các ngươi lừa dối các ngươi, cũng đừng nghe các giấc mộng mà các ngươi khiến [chúng] mơ thấy.
vi.B: Vì {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân, Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên, phán như vầy: Đừng để các nhà tiên tri và các thầy bói ở giữa các ngươi lừa dối các ngươi, cũng đừng nghe những giấc mộng mà các ngươi xúi chúng mơ thấy.
vi.R: Đây là lời {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân, Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên, phán: Đừng để các nhà tiên tri và các thầy bói ở giữa các ngươi lừa gạt các ngươi. Đừng nghe những giấc mộng mà các ngươi muốn chúng mơ thấy cho các ngươi.

ko.L: 이스라엘의 하나님 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이와 같이 말씀하신다. 너희 가운데 있는 너희 예언자들과 너희 점쟁이들에게 속지 말고, 너희가 꾸게 하는 너희 꿈에 귀를 기울이지 마라.
ko.B: 이스라엘의 하나님 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이렇게 말씀하신다. 너희 가운데 있는 예언자들과 점쟁이들에게 속지 마라. 너희가 그들에게 꾸어 달라고 조르는 꿈에 귀를 기울이지 마라.
ko.R: 이스라엘의 하나님, 하늘의 군대를 거느리신 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 하시는 말씀이다. 너희 가운데 있는 예언자들과 점쟁이들에게 속지 마라. 너희가 그들에게 꾸어 달라고 하는 꿈 이야기에 귀를 기울이지 마라.

pt.L: Pois assim diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos, o Deus de Israel: Não deixem que os enganem os seus profetas que [estão] no meio de vocês e os seus adivinhos, e não deem ouvidos aos sonhos que vocês os fazem sonhar.
pt.B: Pois assim diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos, o Deus de Israel: Não deixem que os profetas e os adivinhos que estão entre vocês os enganem, e não deem ouvidos aos sonhos que vocês os incentivam a sonhar.
pt.R: É isto que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos, o Deus de Israel, diz: Não deixem que os profetas e os que leem a sorte entre vocês os enganem. Não deem ouvidos aos sonhos que vocês querem que eles sonhem para vocês.

decisions.choice: your prophets and your diviners: the prophets the people chose and listened to
decisions.reason: "Your" prophets are those the people themselves follow, not men God has sent (verse 9; 27:9). Diviners tried to learn the future by signs and omens, a practice the law forbids (Deuteronomy 18:10-14). Putting the two side by side shows what these prophets really were.

decisions.choice: deceive: lead astray with false hopes
decisions.reason: The verb means to deceive or delude. It is the word the Assyrian envoy used when he warned Jerusalem not to let Hezekiah deceive them (2 Kings 18:29; Isaiah 36:14), and the word Jeremiah used when he accused God of letting the people be deceived by promises of peace (4:10).

decisions.choice: the dreams which you are causing to dream: dreams the people prompt others to have
decisions.reason: The verb form is causative: "which you cause to be dreamed". It seems to mean that the people's own wishes encourage the prophets to dream what they want to hear. Some take the form as an unusual way of saying "which you dream", which would make the dreams the people's own. The sense of the warning is the same: they are not to trust dreams that tell them what they want.

decisions.choice: dreams: a recognized way of receiving a message from God
decisions.reason: God could speak in dreams (Numbers 12:6; Genesis 37:5-11), but Jeremiah sets the lying dreams of the prophets against the word of the LORD (23:25-32; 27:9).

decisions.choice: the prophets and the diviners who are among you
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the two groups together, as English does, rather than splitting them as the Hebrew does. Readable says "fortune-tellers" for the diviners and "fool" for "deceive".

decisions.choice: that you urge them to dream (Balanced); that you want them to dream for you (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal brackets "them"; Balanced and Readable say how the people cause the dreams, as m3 reads the verb.

source.text: כִּ֣י בְשֶׁ֔קֶר הֵ֛ם נִבְּאִ֥ים לָכֶ֖ם בִּשְׁמִ֑י לֹ֥א שְׁלַחְתִּ֖ים נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: For with falsehood they [are] prophesying to you in my name; not I sent them, declaration of Yahweh.

en.L: For it is falsely that they are prophesying to you in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name; I did not send them, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: For they are prophesying lies to you in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name. I did not send them, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: They are using {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name to tell you lies. I did not send them, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

es.L: Porque con mentira {{plural_you:les|os}} profetizan en {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre; yo no los envié, declara {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.B: Porque {{plural_you:les|os}} profetizan mentiras en {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre. Yo no los envié, afirma {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.R: Están usando {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre para {{plural_you:decirles|deciros}} mentiras. Yo no los envié, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.

fr.L: Car c’est faussement qu’ils vous prophétisent en {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom ; je ne les ai pas envoyés, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.B: Car ils vous prophétisent des mensonges en {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom. Je ne les ai pas envoyés, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.R: Ils se servent de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom pour vous dire des mensonges. Je ne les ai pas envoyés, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.

sw.L: Kwa maana wanawatabiria kwa uongo kwa jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}; sikuwatuma, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.B: Kwa maana wanawatabiria uongo kwa jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}. Sikuwatuma, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.R: Wanalitumia jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} kuwaambia uongo. Sikuwatuma, anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.

vi.L: Vì chúng nhân danh {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói tiên tri giả dối cho các ngươi; {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} không sai chúng, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy.
vi.B: Vì chúng nhân danh {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói tiên tri dối trá cho các ngươi. Ta không hề sai chúng, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy.

decisions.choice: seventy years for Babylon: the time Jeremiah had already named
decisions.reason: Jeremiah had said that the nations would serve the king of Babylon seventy years, and that after that God would punish Babylon (25:11-12). Later readers saw the promise fulfilled when the exiles returned (2 Chronicles 36:21-22; Ezra 1:1), and Daniel prayed over these words (Daniel 9:2).

decisions.choice: for Babylon: the seventy years are the time of Babylon's power
decisions.reason: The years are counted "for Babylon": the span of its rule, not the length of any one group's exile. Babylon's empire lasted from Nebuchadnezzar's victory in 605 BC to the fall of Babylon to Cyrus in 539 BC, close to seventy years; seventy is also the span of a full human life (Psalm 90:10). Either way, the exiles would not be going home soon, against what the prophets were telling them (verses 8-9; 28:3-4).

decisions.choice: I will visit you: I will turn my attention to you, here for your good
decisions.reason: The verb means to take notice of, to attend to someone. It can mean to come to help (Genesis 50:24; Exodus 4:31) or to punish (verse 32). Here it is for good, as the rest of the verse says.

decisions.choice: I will establish my good word: I will make my promise come true
decisions.reason: To "establish" a word is to carry it out (28:6; 33:14). The "good word" is God's promise of return, given in 24:6 and spelled out in the verses that follow.

decisions.choice: come to your aid (Balanced); come and help you (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Visit" in English suggests a social call; Balanced and Readable say what God's visit means here (m3).

decisions.choice: Babylon will rule for seventy years
decisions.reason: Readable says what "for Babylon" means (m2) in a sentence of its own.

decisions.choice: "thăm viếng" (visit)
decisions.reason: Here God's visiting is for good (meaning decision m3), so Literal says "thăm viếng", which in Vietnamese carries kindness; Balanced and Readable say what it means.

decisions.choice: "돌보다" (L); "찾아가 돌보다" (B); "찾아가 돕다" (R) for "visit"
decisions.reason: Here God's "visiting" is for good (meaning decision m3); the same verb "돌보다" was used in 23:2, so the two senses stay linked in Korean.

decisions.choice: plans for you: God's purpose for the exiles as a people
decisions.reason: The "you" is plural and means the exiles of Judah as a community. The promise belongs to the setting of verse 10: after the seventy years God will bring his people back, and the plans of peace are his purpose for the nation's future. Many readers take comfort from the verse for their own lives, and it does show what kind of God he is: his final purpose for his people is good. But it is first a promise to a people in exile, not a pledge of success to each person, and some of those who first heard it would die in Babylon before it came true.

decisions.choice: the plans that I am planning: God's settled intentions
decisions.reason: The noun and the verb come from one root: "the plans I plan". Elsewhere God says that he is planning a plan of disaster against Judah (18:11; compare 49:20; 50:45). Here the same words describe a plan of peace. The participle "I am planning" shows that the plan is already in his mind.

decisions.choice: plans of peace and not of evil: plans for well-being, not for disaster
decisions.reason: "Peace" is the same word as in verse 7: wholeness and well-being. "Evil" here means harm or disaster, not moral wickedness (compare 21:10; 24:5).

decisions.choice: a future and a hope: a hopeful future
decisions.reason: The first word means what comes afterward: the end of a matter, its outcome, the future. With "hope" it may name two things, or one thing in two words: a future full of hope. The same pair is used in 31:17 ("there is hope for your future") and Proverbs 23:18.

decisions.choice: I: said twice, for emphasis
decisions.reason: The pronoun "I" is written out before both verbs, though the verb forms already say "I". The emphasis sets God's knowledge of his own plans against the prophets' claims (verses 8-9).

decisions.choice: what I have planned for you ... I have planned peace for you, not disaster
decisions.reason: Balanced puts the plans in verbs, as English often does, and starts a new sentence for the second half; "know well" carries the emphatic "I" (m5).

decisions.choice: well-being, not trouble; a future and something to hope for
decisions.reason: Readable says "well-being" for "peace", as in verse 7, and gives "hope" as a phrase young readers can follow.

decisions.choice: planes de paz y no de mal ... un futuro y una esperanza (Literal); paz, y no desgracia (Balanced); bienestar, y no problemas (Readable)
decisions.reason: A well-known verse; the wording is drafted from the Hebrew gloss ("plans", "peace and not evil", "a future and a hope") rather than from a familiar version.

decisions.choice: mipango ninayowapangia
decisions.reason: "Mipango" (plans) and "kupanga" give the Hebrew noun and verb from one root, as the English does; the wording is kept apart from the familiar Union Version line.

decisions.choice: "les projets que je forme" (L); "ce que j'ai projeté" (B); "ce que j'ai prévu" (R)
decisions.reason: The noun and verb share one root; French keeps them close ("projets ... projeté", "prévu") and avoids "pensées", which is the wording of well-known versions; Readable repeats "bien-être" from verse 7.

decisions.choice: "bình an ... tai họa"
decisions.reason: "Bình an" is the key term for shalom, as in verse 7; the opposite is the "tai họa" of 18:8, not wickedness. This well-known verse is drafted from the Hebrew, not from a familiar version.

decisions.choice: "평안 ... 재앙" (L, B); "평안 ... 괴로움" (R)
decisions.reason: "Plans of *shalom* and not of evil" means well-being, not disaster (meaning decision m3); "재앙" keeps God from being heard planning wickedness, as in 18:8. The verse is widely known; the wording was drafted from the Hebrew and checked against familiar versions.

decisions.choice: projetos que estou projetando (L); o que planejei ... é paz, e não desgraça (B); bem-estar, e não sofrimento (R)
alternatives: os planos que tenho para vocês
decisions.reason: This well-known verse is drafted from the Hebrew, in this translation's own words, not in the familiar wording of other Portuguese Bibles. Literal keeps the noun and verb of one root (m2) with "projetos que estou projetando"; Balanced puts the plans in a verb, as the English does. "Paz" is the shalom of verse 7 (m3) and "mal", "desgraça" the harm, not wickedness, as 21:10 has it. The "vocês" is the exiles as a people (m1).

decisions.choice: and you will call: what will follow from God's plans
decisions.reason: The verbs carry on from verses 10-11 and describe what the people will do when God turns to them. It is not a condition laid down first; God's promise and the people's turning to him go together.

decisions.choice: you will pray to me and I will listen: the prayer of the exiles
decisions.reason: Solomon asked that when Israel was taken captive to an enemy land, and prayed to God there, God would hear and forgive them (1 Kings 8:46-50). Moses said that in exile they would turn back to God (Deuteronomy 4:29-31; 30:1-3).

decisions.choice: come: come to God in prayer
alternatives: walk, set out (on the way back)
decisions.reason: The verb "go" or "come" stands between "call" and "pray" and means coming before God; some take it as setting out on the way home, but it most likely belongs with the prayer.

decisions.choice: Then
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable show with "Then" that this follows from verses 10-11. Balanced says "hear" for the last verb, which in Hebrew is "listen" and also "answer".

decisions.reason: Moses foretold that in exile Israel would seek the LORD and find him, when they searched for him with all their heart and soul (Deuteronomy 4:29). The letter uses the same two verbs for seeking and the same "with all your heart": what Moses foretold is now about to happen.

decisions.choice: when: the condition for finding
decisions.reason: The word can mean "when", "if" or "because", as in Deuteronomy 4:29. Wholehearted seeking is the way God is found.

decisions.choice: with all your heart: with the whole mind and will
decisions.reason: The heart is the center of thought and will. To seek with all the heart is to seek with nothing held back (Deuteronomy 6:5; Jeremiah 24:7).

decisions.choice: seek, search for (Balanced); look for (Readable)
decisions.reason: Each level follows its wording of Deuteronomy 4:29 so that the echo can be heard. Literal brackets the second "me", which the Hebrew leaves out.

decisions.choice: "vous me trouverez", with no brackets
decisions.reason: The Hebrew leaves out the second "me"; French needs the object pronoun before the verb, where brackets would break the word order, so Literal writes it plainly.

decisions.choice: I will be found by you: I will let myself be found
decisions.reason: The verb form means that God allows himself to be found by those who seek him (Isaiah 55:6; 65:1; 1 Chronicles 28:9). Finding him is his gift, not the seeker's achievement.

decisions.choice: I will turn your captivity: I will restore your fortunes
alternatives: I will bring back your captives
decisions.reason: The phrase is literally "turn your turning". It can mean to bring back the captives, and so it was long translated "turn your captivity", but it is also used where there is no captivity (Job 42:10) and means to restore what was lost, to turn a people's lot around. In this verse both senses fit, since the captives are to be brought home.

decisions.choice: your fortunes: the form read aloud
decisions.reason: The written consonants (ketiv) have a slightly different form of the noun; the scribes marked the more usual form to be read aloud (qere). The meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: from all the nations and all the places: a scattering wider than Babylon
decisions.reason: The promise looks beyond the exiles in Babylon to all of Israel's scattered people, as Moses foretold (Deuteronomy 30:3-4; compare 23:3).

decisions.choice: the Greek has a shorter verse
decisions.reason: The Greek translation has only "and I will appear to you" and lacks the rest of the verse. The Hebrew is followed.

decisions.choice: I will let you find me
decisions.reason: Balanced turns the passive "be found by you" into an active sentence, as English prefers.

decisions.choice: make things good again for you; scattered
decisions.reason: Readable says what "restore your fortunes" means (m2) and says "scattered" for "driven".

decisions.choice: restauraré su suerte (Literal, Balanced); Haré que todo vuelva a ir bien (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Restore the fortunes" keeps the wording the terms note sets (Psalm 14:7; Psalm 126:4).

decisions.choice: nitawarudishia mafanikio yenu (Literal, Balanced); nitayafanya mambo yenu kuwa mema tena (Readable)
decisions.reason: The wording used for *shuv shevut* ("restore the fortunes") in this block, as the English note sets: the whole restoration, not only the return of captives.

decisions.choice: "je rétablirai votre sort" (L, B); "je rendrai votre situation de nouveau heureuse" (R)
decisions.reason: Shuv shevut as the Jeremiah note sets it: "restore the fortunes" at Literal and Balanced, "make things good again" at Readable.

decisions.choice: "phục hồi cơ đồ" (L, B); "làm cho mọi sự tốt đẹp trở lại" (R) for shuv shevut
decisions.reason: One wording for "restore the fortunes" at each level, used where it returns in 30-33. "Cơ đồ" covers a people's whole state and wealth, as the meaning decision reads it, not only the return of captives; "trở về" is kept for coming home.

decisions.choice: "운명을 돌이키다" (L); "형편을 회복시키다" (B); "다시 잘되게 해 주다" (R) for *shuv shevut*
decisions.reason: The wording for "restore the fortunes" through Jeremiah (29:14 to 49:39), one form per level (meaning decision m2). Literal follows the English "restore the fortunes" rather than "turn the captivity"; Balanced and Readable say what it means.

decisions.choice: me deixarei achar (no span); restaurarei a sorte (L, B)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the passive with a reflexive, "eu me deixarei achar" (m1); that "me" goes with the subject "eu", which takes no span, so the English "myself" span has none here. Balanced and Readable say "que vocês me achem", with the span, as the English does. "Restaurar a sorte" (L, B) is the wording of Deuteronomy 30:3 in Portuguese for the phrase (m2).
